newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican authorities bounce Czech cactus smugglers.
newsitem.headline: Mexican authorities bounce Czech cactus smugglers.

text.p: Ten Czech citizens were arrested in northern Mexico after being caught with 300 rare wild cactus plants in danger of extinction and 5,000 seeds, Mexico's Federal Environmental Protection Agency said on Wednesday.
The Czechs can be fined up to 100,000 pesos ($12,695) for each plant and seed, the government agency said.

"The agency began prosecuting the 10 people from the Czech Republic who had in their possession cactus seeds and fruit and wild cactus that they presumably intended to carry out of the country for individual collections," agency spokesman Jose Luis Tamez told Reuters.
Each cactus plant and seed can fetch $2,000 from private collectors, according to the agency.
Detained by rural police, the Czechs said they were studying the native flora. Last week two other Czechs were caught picking the same species of cactus.

The wild cactus plants are on the brink of extinction and only found in northern Nuevo Leon state, the agency said. Cactus picking is generally prohibited by Mexican law, while the collection of wild fauna requires official permission.
